title: Marcos thanks Pinoys for patience during ASEAN meet
summary: President Marcos thanked the Filipino people for their “patience, understanding and cooperation” during the country’s hosting of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations Summit…

blocks.text: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. speaks during a press briefing at the International Media Center in Pasay City on November 17, 2026)

MANILA, Philippines — President Marcos thanked the Filipino people for their “patience, understanding and cooperation” during the country’s hosting of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit and related summits this year.?

“I also wish to express my special thanks to the Filipino people, particularly those whose daily routines were affected by the preparations and activities surrounding the summit,” Marcos said on Tuesday.?
“For that warmth and generosity you have shown our guests, you have once again demonstrated the hospitality for which Filipinos are known around the world,” the President said.?

The Chief Executive likewise expressed his gratitude to government agencies, personnel and volunteers for their contribution to the country’s successful hosting of the bi-annual meeting of the 11-member regional bloc.?
“This was the product of the hard work and dedication of a multitude of people and agencies, each of whom played an important role in making this summit a success,” Marcos said.?
On Tuesday, the Philippines formally turned over the chairship of ASEAN to Singapore during the culmination of the summit at the Philippine International Convention Center in Pasay City.
Senators lauded the hosting of the ASEAN Summit even as the President’s sister, Sen. Imee Marcos, questioned the “prudence and proportionality” of the reported P22.9-billion cost for the chairship.
Sen. Erwin Tulfo questioned his colleague’s assessment of the ASEAN Summit based on its costs, as he pushed for evaluating the summit on “outcomes and commitments that will benefit our country soon.”

Reacting to the hundreds arrested for protesting Trump’s visit and the US-led artificial intelligence supply chain initiative Pax Silica, Sen. Panfilo Lacson cited his experience as former national police chief in believing authorities have intelligence to “handle the protests.”
Speaker Faustino Dy III urged lawmakers from Southeast Asian nations to work on legislation meant to increase trade and other avenues of cooperation as a bid to strengthen regional unity.
Meanwhile, the Department of Health said two very important delegates required medical assistance during the ASEAN Summit. — Marc Jayson Cayabyab, Rhodina Villanueva, Daphne Galvez
